checks.name: Global ordering
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal global_ordering
checks.output: 3 tests pass. The deterministic matrix executes 36 unique identifier pairs: 15 increasing pairs append, 6 duplicates and 15 decreasing pairs return EventIdNotIncreasing, and every refusal leaves the one-event seed unchanged. The fixed examples separately prove later recovery after refused ids and atomic refusal.

checks.name: Revision algebra
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal revision_algebra
checks.output: 5 tests pass. First revision, exact successors, gaps, repeats and per-aggregate independence are covered. Journal::append delegates to validate_revision_successor, which uses Revision::checked_next; u64::MAX yields typed RevisionExhausted { current, observed } rather than panic, wrap or overwrite.

checks.name: Schema independence
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal schema_independence
checks.output: 4 tests pass. Reader-supplied event decode ranges fail closed below and above their inclusive bounds independently of table schema. EventSchemaVersion rejects zero. DomainEvent now owns a distinct DomainEventPayload newtype; empty, control-bearing and over-4096-byte payloads are unrepresentable.

checks.name: Outcome vocabulary
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal outcome_vocabulary
checks.output: 5 tests pass. An exhaustive match names the six required variants and exact wire spellings. Unknown means transport uncertainty while Rejected means the operation did not happen; the two are distinct and cannot be conflated by the API.

checks.name: Idempotency exactness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal idempotency_exactness
checks.output: 9 tests pass. The deterministic matrix executes 81 target/payload pairs: 9 exact replays return the identical original receipt, 18 changed-payload cases return IdempotencyPayloadConflict, and 54 changed-target cases return IdempotencyConflict. Every conflict leaves the seed receipt unchanged. ActionTarget is an owned bounded newtype stored directly in ActionReceipt; string entry points are validation adapters into the typed core.

checks.name: Receipt durability
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal receipt_durability && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --doc journal
checks.output: 3 behavioural tests pass plus the journal doc suite at 7 positive and 8 compile-fail cases. Receipts own every field, remain queryable after the request scope and ledger end, and take no lifetime argument; ActionReceipt<'connection> does not compile.

checks.name: Cursor monotonicity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal cursor_monotonicity
checks.output: 10 tests pass against accepted A2. Cursors are keyed by consumer and topic, advance idempotently forward, return CursorWentBackwards without mutation on rewind, and resync both below and above first..=caught_up with bounded snapshot coordinates. caught_up uses saturating_add(1), so a range ending at u64::MAX neither wraps nor invents a position. Limit L2 is retained: when representable, last+1 is the live caught-up boundary rather than an event.

checks.name: Replay purity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test journal replay_purity && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --doc journal
checks.output: 5 behavioural tests pass plus the journal doc suite at 7 positive and 8 compile-fail cases against accepted A1. Replay takes only a projection, grants shared event access, and exposes no constructible Outbox: named extra-argument, widened-callback, mutable-event, private-field and Default routes fail compilation. API inspection finds no exported Outbox constructor, From implementation or returning function. The measured L1 counterexample intentionally sends event ids [1,2,3] through a projection-owned channel, demonstrating that replay confers no capability but cannot make an already-capable projection pure.

Plan, program and guide verification pass. The harness accepts the exact two implementation paths as candidate_ready. rust/Cargo.lock is unchanged at SHA-256 420793404861e0bfadfeaa8677ec090099076967be9ef605a15a8656a5fe0fe4; no manifest or dependency changed.

review.acceptance: independent read-only verification recommends exact-tree completion

compatibility: Existing string-taking ActionLedger entry points and ActionReceipt::target remain available as adapters/views; the typed core is additive. DomainEvent::new gains its contract-required payload argument. No database, transport, outbox delivery or table-schema behavior is introduced.
provenance: Only permitted repository requirements, the accepted A1/A2 owner decision, current clean-room product code and synthetic test matrices were used. No prior implementation source, private archive, network input, credential, private identifier or customer data was accessed.
limits: L1 remains explicit: a projection may use a capability it already owns; replay only guarantees that this crate confers none.
L2 remains explicit: when representable, the caught-up cursor boundary last+1 is live although it is not a retained event.
Table-level transactionality remains deferred to R4 because this value-type slice opens no store or transaction.
